title: 12.1 Motivation
text: densityHeatmap() visualizes a list of distributions using kernel density estimates mapped to colors: import numpy as np import pandas as pd import complexheatmap as ch rng = np.random.default_rng(123) mat = pd.DataFrame(rng.normal(size=(50, 10)), columns=list("abcdefghij")) ch.ht_opt.HEATMAP_LEGEND_PADDING = ch.unit(14, "mm") ch.draw(ch.densityHeatmap(mat, title="Density heatmap"), padding=ch.unit([4, 18, 4, 4], "mm")) Density heatmap baseline frequencyHeatmap() provides a histogram-binned counterpart, supporting "count", "proportion", and "density" statistics: ch.ht_opt(RESET=True) ch.draw(ch.frequencyHeatmap(mat, title="Frequency heatmap (2D)")) 2D frequency heatmap A 2D frequency heatmap does not immediately look like a 3D histogram. Passing use_3d=True renders each bin as an isometric 3D bar whose height is proportional to the cell value: ch.ht_opt.TITLE_PADDING = ch.unit([10, 2], "mm") ch.ht_opt.HEATMAP_LEGEND_PADDING = ch.unit(8, "mm") fh3d = ch.frequencyHeatmap( mat, use_3d=True, title="Frequency heatmap (use_3d=True)", top_annotation=ch.HeatmapAnnotation( _spacer=ch.anno_empty(border=False, height=ch.unit(6, "mm")), show_annotation_name=False, ), bar_max_length=ch.unit(8, "mm"), ) ch.draw(fh3d, padding=ch.unit([4, 10, 6, 6], "mm")) 3D frequency heatmap with isometric bars

title: 12.2 Implementation of 3D heatmap
text: 3D heatmaps are built on the bar3D() primitive, which draws an isometric rectangular prism onto the active grid viewport: ch.grid_newpage(width_in=3.5, height_in=3.0) ch.bar3D(x=0.5, y=0.5, w=0.2, h=0.2, l=ch.unit(1, "cm"), theta=60) Single isometric 3D bar drawn by bar3D The geometric parameters of bar3D() are illustrated below: x, y: Center coordinates of the bottom face (defaults to "npc" if numeric). w, h: Width (x-axis) and height (y-axis) of the bottom face. l: Projected length of the bar along the z-axis. theta: Projection angle in degrees, constrained to [0, 90]. Isometric projection geometry of bar3D To enhance depth perception, bar3D() automatically computes three distinct face brightness levels using add_luminance() in HCL color space: ch.grid_newpage(width_in=6.0, height_in=2.2) ch.bar3D( x=np.linspace(0.2, 0.8, 4), y=0.35, w=ch.unit(6, "mm"), h=ch.unit(6, "mm"), l=ch.unit(1.1, "cm"), fill=["red", "green", "blue", "purple"], ) 3D bars with add_luminance shading across three visible faces In ComplexHeatmap-py, bar3D() accepts a scalar theta angle per call (between 0 and 90). Drawing across multiple angles simply iterates over (x, theta) pairs: ch.grid_newpage(width_in=6.4, height_in=2.4) for x_pos, th in zip(np.linspace(0.18, 0.78, 4), [20.0, 40.0, 60.0, 80.0]): ch.bar3D(x=float(x_pos), y=0.32, w=ch.unit(6, "mm"), h=ch.unit(6, "mm"), l=ch.unit(1.1, "cm"), theta=th, fill="#4DAF4A") ch.grid_text(f"theta={int(th)}°", x=float(x_pos), y=0.14, just="top", gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=9.5)) 3D bar projection angles from 20 to 80 degrees Heatmap3D() wraps Heatmap() with a vectorized layer_fun that draws bar3D() bars back-to-front across each heatmap slice. The input matrix must be non-negative, row names default to "left", and dendrograms are hidden by default (show_row_dend=False, show_column_dend=False) while clustering still runs: mat3d = pd.DataFrame( np.random.default_rng(7).uniform(0.0, 1.0, size=(10, 10)), index=list("ABCDEFGHIJ"), columns=list("abcdefghij"), ) ch.draw(ch.Heatmap3D(mat3d, name="mat", column_title="This is a 3D heatmap")) Basic Heatmap3D where tall top/right bars overlap title and legend Because 3D bars project upward and to the right, tall bars near the top or right edges can overlap the column title or legend. You can prevent overlap by adjusting ht_opt.HEATMAP_LEGEND_PADDING and ht_opt.TITLE_PADDING, and optionally inserting a transparent _spacer top annotation (anno_empty(border=False)) to reserve extra overhead clearance: ch.ht_opt.HEATMAP_LEGEND_PADDING = ch.unit(8, "mm") ch.ht_opt.TITLE_PADDING = ch.unit([10, 2], "mm") ht_pad = ch.Heatmap3D( mat3d, name="mat", column_title="3D heatmap with adjusted padding", top_annotation=ch.HeatmapAnnotation( _spacer=ch.anno_empty(border=False, height=ch.unit(7, "mm")), show_annotation_name=False, ), bar_max_length=ch.unit(8, "mm"), ) ch.draw(ht_pad, padding=ch.unit([4, 4, 6, 6], "mm")) ch.ht_opt(RESET=True) Heatmap3D with spacer annotation and global padding adjustments Heatmap3D() supports standard Heatmap() features such as row_split, column_split, bar_rel_width, bar_rel_height, and bar_max_length: ch.ht_opt.HEATMAP_LEGEND_PADDING = ch.unit(8, "mm") ch.ht_opt.TITLE_PADDING = ch.unit([8, 2], "mm") ht_split = ch.Heatmap3D( mat3d, name="score", col=ch.colorRamp2([0, 0.5, 1], ["#2B8CBE", "#FEE08B", "#D7301F"]), row_split=["Group 1"] * 5 + ["Group 2"] * 5, column_split=["Cond A"] * 5 + ["Cond B"] * 5, bar_rel_width=0.75, bar_rel_height=0.75, bar_max_length=ch.unit(7.5, "mm"), top_annotation=ch.HeatmapAnnotation( _spacer=ch.anno_empty(border=False, height=ch.unit(6, "mm")), show_annotation_name=False, ), row_gap=ch.unit(3, "mm"), column_gap=ch.unit(3, "mm"), ) ch.draw(ht_split, column_title="Split 3D Heatmap", padding=ch.unit([4, 4, 6, 6], "mm")) ch.ht_opt(RESET=True) Split Heatmap3D with custom bar geometry Finally, we apply Heatmap3D() to the bundled measles dataset (compare with the 2D version in Section 14.2): mat = ch.load_dataset("measles") year_text = [str(c) if i

title: 13 Genome-level heatmap
text: ComplexHeatmap-py makes it straightforward to build genome-scale, chromosome-split multi-track heatmaps with lightweight built-in interval classes (IRanges, GRanges), genome binning (bin_genome()), and signal summarization (normalize_genomic_signals_to_bins()).

title: 13.1 Genomic bins and signal normalization
text: In a genome-level heatmap, each row (for vertical chromosome layout) or column (for horizontal chromosome layout) represents a uniform genomic bin. IRanges and GRanges store 1-based closed genomic intervals [start, end], and bin_genome() partitions built-in reference assemblies ("hg19", "hg38", "mm10", "mm9") into fixed-width windows: import numpy as np import pandas as pd import complexheatmap as ch chrs = [f"chr{i}" for i in range(1, 23)] chr_window = ch.bin_genome("hg19", bin_size=1_000_000, chromosomes=chrs) print(chr_window) # GRanges(n=2897, mcols=[]) Next, genomic signal intervals must be aggregated into the chr_window bins. normalize_genomic_signals_to_bins() overlaps chr_window against signal intervals via findOverlaps() and summarizes overlapping values: Overlapping model between a genomic window and signal regions For a given genomic bin of width W + W' where n signal intervals intersect the window with intersection widths w_i (W = sum(w_i)) and signal values x_i, normalize_genomic_signals_to_bins() provides four numeric method options: "weighted" (default): width-weighted mean over intersected segments, v_w = sum(x_i * w_i) / sum(w_i). "absolute": unweighted mean over overlapping signal intervals, v_a = sum(x_i) / n. "w0": weighted mean blending the intersected signal and uncovered background (0), v_w0 = (v_w * W) / (W + W'). "number": count of overlapping signal intervals per bin (n). For categorical signals (such as copy-number states "gain" and "loss"), we can pick the category with the largest total overlap width per bin using findOverlaps(): def bin_categorical_signals(window: ch.GRanges, gr: ch.GRanges, labels: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray: """Assign each genomic bin the category with largest total overlap width.""" out = np.full(len(window), np.nan, dtype=object) qh, sh = ch.findOverlaps(window, gr) if len(qh) == 0: return out ov_w = np.minimum(window.end[qh], gr.end[sh]) - np.maximum(window.start[qh], gr.start[sh]) + 1 by_win: dict[int, dict[str, int]] = {} for q_i, s_i, w_i in zip(qh, sh, ov_w): if w_i <= 0: continue lbl = str(labels[s_i]) bucket = by_win.setdefault(int(q_i), {}) bucket[lbl] = bucket.get(lbl, 0) + int(w_i) for q_i, bucket in by_win.items(): out[q_i] = max(bucket.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])[0] return out

title: 13.2 Horizontal genome-level heatmap
text: We generate synthetic genomic signals across four data types using generateRandomBed(), normalize them onto 1 Mb bins of hg19, and combine them horizontally: bed1 = ch.generateRandomBed(nr=1000, nc=10, species="hg19", seed=123) bed1 = bed1[bed1["chr"].isin(chrs)].reset_index(drop=True) gr1 = ch.GRanges( bed1["chr"].tolist(), ch.IRanges(bed1["start"].to_numpy(), bed1["end"].to_numpy()), **{c: bed1[c].to_numpy() for c in bed1.columns[3:]}, ) num_mat = ch.normalize_genomic_signals_to_bins( gr1, value_column=list(bed1.columns[3:]), bins=chr_window, method="weighted", empty_value=np.nan ).mcols.to_numpy(dtype=float) rng = np.random.default_rng(42) char_cols = [] for j in range(10): bed_c = ch.generateRandomBed(nr=1000, nc=0, species="hg19", seed=100 + j) bed_c = bed_c[bed_c["chr"].isin(chrs)].sample(n=20, random_state=100 + j).reset_index(drop=True) cnv_vals = rng.choice(["gain", "loss"], size=len(bed_c)) gr_c = ch.GRanges(bed_c["chr"].tolist(), ch.IRanges(bed_c["start"].to_numpy(), bed_c["end"].to_numpy())) char_cols.append(bin_categorical_signals(chr_window, gr_c, cnv_vals)) char_mat = np.column_stack(char_cols) bed2 = ch.generateRandomBed(nr=120, nc=2, species="hg19", seed=456) bed2 = bed2[bed2["chr"].isin(chrs)].reset_index(drop=True) gr2 = ch.GRanges( bed2["chr"].tolist(), ch.IRanges(bed2["start"].to_numpy(), bed2["end"].to_numpy()), v1=bed2["value1"].to_numpy(), v2=bed2["value2"].to_numpy(), ) v_mat = ch.normalize_genomic_signals_to_bins( gr2, ["v1", "v2"], bins=chr_window, method="weighted", empty_value=np.nan ).mcols.to_numpy(dtype=float) bed3 = ch.generateRandomBed(nr=45, nc=0, species="hg19", seed=789) bed3 = bed3[bed3["chr"].isin(chrs)].reset_index(drop=True) gr3 = ch.GRanges( bed3["chr"].tolist(), ch.IRanges(bed3["start"].to_numpy(), bed3["start"].to_numpy()), gene=[f"gene_{k + 1}" for k in range(len(bed3))], ) qh, sh = ch.findOverlaps(chr_window, gr3) at = qh.tolist() labels = gr3.mcols["gene"].iloc[sh].tolist() We preserve natural chromosome ordering (chr1..chr22) with an ordered pd.Categorical and pass row_title="%s" so each chromosome slice is labeled: chr_cat = pd.Categorical(chr_window.seqnames, categories=chrs, ordered=True) subgroup = ["A"] * 5 + ["B"] * 5 bar_vals = np.nan_to_num(v_mat[:, 0], nan=0.0) bar_cols = ["#DF536B" if val > 0 else "#61D04F" for val in bar_vals] with ch.ht_opt.local(TITLE_PADDING=ch.unit([4, 4], "points")): ht_list = ( ch.Heatmap( num_mat, name="mat", col=ch.colorRamp2([-1, 0, 1], ["green", "white", "red"]), row_split=chr_cat, row_title="%s", cluster_rows=False, show_column_dend=False, column_split=subgroup, cluster_column_slices=False, column_title="numeric matrix", top_annotation=ch.HeatmapAnnotation( subgroup=subgroup, col={"subgroup": {"A": "#E41A1C", "B": "#377EB8"}}, annotation_name_side="left", ), row_title_rot=0, row_title_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=9), border=True, row_gap=ch.unit(0, "points"), ) + ch.Heatmap( char_mat, name="CNV", col={"gain": "red", "loss": "blue"}, na_col="white", border=True, cluster_columns=False, column_title="character matrix", ) + ch.rowAnnotation(label=ch.anno_mark(at=at, labels=labels, labels_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=7))) + ch.rowAnnotation( pt=ch.anno_points(v_mat, gp=ch.gpar(col=["#2297E6", "#28E2E5"]), pch=[1, 16], size=ch.unit(1.5, "mm")), width=ch.unit(2, "cm"), ) + ch.rowAnnotation( bar=ch.anno_barplot(bar_vals, gp=ch.gpar(col=bar_cols, fill=bar_cols)), width=ch.unit(2, "cm"), ) ) ch.draw(ht_list, width=8.8, height=10.5, padding=ch.unit([12, 16, 4, 4], "mm"), merge_legends=True) Horizontal genome-level multi-track heatmap across hg19 autosomes

title: 13.3 Vertical genome-level heatmap
text:
Transposing the matrices (num_mat.T, char_mat.T), swapping row_* and column_* parameters, and concatenating vertically with % ch.v % produces a horizontal chromosome layout. Staggering neighbor chromosome titles with 
 prevents label collisions on shorter chromosomes (chr16–chr22). Note also that ComplexHeatmap-py uses "legend_direction": "horizontal" inside heatmap_legend_param and annotation_legend_param: alt_titles = [f"
{c}" if (idx + 1) % 2 == 0 else f"{c}
" for idx, c in enumerate(chrs)] with ch.ht_opt.local(TITLE_PADDING=ch.unit([4, 4], "points")): ht_vert = ( ch.Heatmap( num_mat.T, name="mat", col=ch.colorRamp2([-1, 0, 1], ["green", "white", "red"]), column_split=chr_cat, cluster_columns=False, show_row_dend=False, row_split=subgroup, cluster_row_slices=False, row_title="numeric matrix", left_annotation=ch.rowAnnotation( subgroup=subgroup, col={"subgroup": {"A": "#E41A1C", "B": "#377EB8"}}, show_annotation_name=False, annotation_legend_param={"subgroup": {"legend_direction": "horizontal", "title_position": "lefttop", "nrow": 1}}, ), column_title_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=7.5), border=True, column_gap=ch.unit(0, "points"), column_title=alt_titles, heatmap_legend_param={"legend_direction": "horizontal", "title_position": "lefttop"}, ) % ch.v % ch.Heatmap( char_mat.T, name="CNV", col={"gain": "red", "loss": "blue"}, na_col="white", border=True, cluster_rows=False, row_title="character matrix", heatmap_legend_param={"legend_direction": "horizontal", "title_position": "lefttop", "nrow": 1}, ) % ch.v % ch.HeatmapAnnotation(label=ch.anno_mark(at=at, labels=labels, side="bottom", labels_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=7))) % ch.v % ch.HeatmapAnnotation( pt=ch.anno_points(v_mat, gp=ch.gpar(col=["#2297E6", "#28E2E5"]), pch=[1, 16], size=ch.unit(1.5, "mm")), annotation_name_side="left", height=ch.unit(2, "cm"), ) % ch.v % ch.HeatmapAnnotation( bar=ch.anno_barplot(bar_vals, gp=ch.gpar(col=bar_cols, fill=bar_cols)), annotation_name_side="left", height=ch.unit(2, "cm"), ) ) ch.draw(ht_vert, width=11.2, height=7.8, padding=ch.unit([4, 4, 6, 8], "mm"), heatmap_legend_side="bottom", merge_legends=True) Vertical genome-level multi-track heatmap

title:
13.4 Chromosome block headers and multi-track
genomic features
text: When displaying chromosome-split multi-omics heatmaps (such as the bundled gr dataset containing 2,415 regions with methylation, expression, genomic feature classes, enhancer overlaps, and correlation scores), anno_block() creates clean colored chromosome header strips alongside row_gap=unit(1, "mm"): gr_df = ch.load_dataset("gr") chrs_10 = [f"chr{i}" for i in range(1, 11)] bins_ref = ch.bin_genome("hg19", bin_size=1_000_000, chromosomes=chrs_10) chr_counts = pd.Series(bins_ref.seqnames).value_counts().reindex(chrs_10).to_numpy(dtype=float) counts = np.floor((chr_counts / chr_counts.sum()) * len(gr_df)).astype(int) counts[0] += len(gr_df) - int(counts.sum()) chr_cat_10 = pd.Categorical(np.concatenate([np.repeat(c, k) for c, k in zip(chrs_10, counts)]), categories=chrs_10, ordered=True) meth_mat = gr_df[[f"meth_s{i}" for i in range(1, 13)]].to_numpy(dtype=float) expr_mat = gr_df[[f"expr_s{i}" for i in range(1, 13)]].to_numpy(dtype=float) enh_mat = gr_df[["weak_enhancer", "strong_enhancer"]].to_numpy(dtype=float) cor_p_raw = gr_df["cor_p"].to_numpy(dtype=float) cor_p = np.nan_to_num(cor_p_raw, nan=0.0, posinf=float(np.nanmax(cor_p_raw[np.isfinite(cor_p_raw)])), neginf=0.0) sample_grp = ["Tumor"] * 6 + ["Control"] * 6 chr_pal = ["#1B9E77", "#D95F02", "#7570B3", "#E7298A", "#66A61E", "#E6AB02", "#A6761D", "#666666", "#377EB8", "#E41A1C"] ht_gr = ( ch.rowAnnotation( chr=ch.anno_block( gp=ch.gpar(fill=chr_pal, col="white"), labels=chrs_10, labels_gp=ch.gpar(col="white", fontsize=8, fontface="bold"), labels_rot=0, width=ch.unit(12, "mm"), ), show_annotation_name=False, ) + ch.Heatmap( meth_mat, name="Methylation", col=ch.colorRamp2([0, 0.5, 1], ["#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"]), row_split=chr_cat_10, cluster_rows=False, cluster_row_slices=False, row_title=None, row_gap=ch.unit(1, "mm"), top_annotation=ch.HeatmapAnnotation( Group=sample_grp, col={"Group": {"Tumor": "#E41A1C", "Control": "#377EB8"}}, annotation_name_side="left", ), column_title="Methylation", show_row_names=False, show_column_names=False, border=True, ) + ch.Heatmap( expr_mat, name="Expression", col=ch.colorRamp2([-2, 0, 2], ["#1B7837", "white", "#762A83"]), column_title="Expression", show_row_names=False, show_column_names=False, border=True, ) + ch.Heatmap( gr_df["annotation"].tolist(), name="Feature", col={"Intergenic": "#FDB462", "intron": "#80B1D3", "others": "#B3DE69"}, width=ch.unit(6, "mm"), ) + ch.rowAnnotation( enhancer=ch.anno_points(enh_mat, gp=ch.gpar(col=["#377EB8", "#E41A1C"]), pch=[1, 16], size=ch.unit(1.2, "mm")), cor_p=ch.anno_barplot(cor_p, gp=ch.gpar(fill="#555555", col="#555555")), gap=ch.unit(4, "mm"), width=ch.unit(4.0, "cm"), ) ) ch.draw( ht_gr, width=10.5, height=8.8, padding=ch.unit([12, 4, 4, 4], "mm"), merge_legends=True, column_title="Multi-track Genomic Regions with Chromosome Block Headers", ) Multi-track genomic heatmap with anno_block chromosome headers

title: 14 More Examples
text: This chapter walks through six complete multi-omics and biological visualization case studies ported to ComplexHeatmap-py.

title:
14.1 Add more information for gene expression
matrix
text: Gene expression heatmaps typically display z-score normalized relative expression across samples. Adding side-by-side absolute expression (base mean), gene length (anno_points), gene biotype (gene type), cluster summary plots (anno_summary()), and k-means cluster indicator strips (anno_block()) puts all gene-level context into one aligned figure: import re import numpy as np import complexheatmap as ch expr = ch.load_dataset("gene_expression") cell_cols = [c for c in expr.columns if "cell" in c] mat = expr[cell_cols].to_numpy(dtype=float) base_mean = mat.mean(axis=1) mat_scaled = ((mat.T - mat.mean(axis=1)) / mat.std(axis=1, ddof=1)).T sample_type = [re.sub(r"s\d+_", "", c) for c in cell_cols] ha = ch.HeatmapAnnotation( type=sample_type, col={"type": {"cell01": "#E41A1C", "cell02": "#377EB8", "cell03": "#4DAF4A"}}, annotation_name_side="left", ) ht_list = ( ch.rowAnnotation( block=ch.anno_block(gp=ch.gpar(fill=[2, 3, 4, 5, 6], col=None)), width=ch.unit(2.5, "mm"), show_annotation_name=False, ) + ch.Heatmap( mat_scaled, name="expression", row_km=5, col=ch.colorRamp2([-2, 0, 2], ["green", "white", "red"]), top_annotation=ha, show_column_names=False, row_title=None, show_row_dend=False, ) + ch.Heatmap( base_mean, name="base mean", top_annotation=ch.HeatmapAnnotation( summary=ch.anno_summary(gp=ch.gpar(fill=[2, 3, 4, 5, 6]), height=ch.unit(2, "cm")), show_annotation_name=False, ), width=ch.unit(15, "mm"), ) + ch.rowAnnotation( length=ch.anno_points( expr["length"].to_numpy(dtype=float), pch=16, size=ch.unit(1, "mm"), axis_param={"at": [0, 2e5, 4e5, 6e5], "labels": ["0kb", "200kb", "400kb", "600kb"]}, width=ch.unit(2.2, "cm"), ) ) + ch.Heatmap( expr["type"].to_numpy(), name="gene type", col={"protein_coding": "#FC8D62", "others": "#8DA0CB", "antisense": "#E78AC3", "pseudogene": "#A6D854"}, top_annotation=ch.HeatmapAnnotation( summary=ch.anno_summary(height=ch.unit(2, "cm")), show_annotation_name=False, ), width=ch.unit(15, "mm"), ) ) ch.draw(ht_list, width=10.8, height=8.2, padding=ch.unit([12, 10, 4, 4], "mm"), ht_gap=ch.unit(3.5, "mm")) Integrated gene expression heatmap with k-means cluster summaries and gene attributes

title: 14.2 The measles vaccine heatmap
text: This classic visualization reproduces the US measles incidence heatmap (1930–2001) using ch.load_dataset("measles"), augmented with yearly and per-state total barplots and a dashed vertical marker at 1961 via decorate_heatmap_body(): mat = ch.load_dataset("measles") arr = mat.to_numpy(dtype=float) ha1 = ch.HeatmapAnnotation( dist1=ch.anno_barplot( arr.sum(axis=0), bar_width=1.0, gp=ch.gpar(col="white", fill="#FFE200"), border=False, axis_param={"at": [0, 2e5, 4e5, 6e5, 8e5], "labels": ["0", "200k", "400k", "600k", "800k"]}, height=ch.unit(2, "cm"), ), show_annotation_name=False, ) ha2 = ch.rowAnnotation( dist2=ch.anno_barplot( arr.sum(axis=1), bar_width=1.0, gp=ch.gpar(col="white", fill="#FFE200"), border=False, axis_param={"at": [0, 5e5, 1e6, 1.5e6], "labels": ["0", "500k", "1m", "1.5m"]}, width=ch.unit(2, "cm"), ), show_annotation_name=False, ) year_text = [str(c) if int(c) % 10 == 0 else "" for c in mat.columns] ha_column = ch.HeatmapAnnotation( year=ch.anno_text(year_text, rot=0, location=ch.unit(1, "npc"), just="top", gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=9)), show_annotation_name=False, ) col_fun = ch.colorRamp2([0, 800, 1000, 127000], ["white", "cornflowerblue", "yellow", "red"]) ht_list = ( ch.Heatmap( mat, name="cases", col=col_fun, cluster_columns=False, show_row_dend=False, rect_gp=ch.gpar(col="white", lwd=0.3), show_column_names=False, row_names_side="left", row_names_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=7.5), column_title="Measles cases in US states 1930-2001\nVaccine introduced 1961", top_annotation=ha1, bottom_annotation=ha_column, heatmap_legend_param={"at": [0, 5e4, 1e5, 1.5e5], "labels": ["0", "50k", "100k", "150k"]}, ) + ha2 ) ch.draw(ht_list, width=11.0, height=9.4, ht_gap=ch.unit(3, "mm"), padding=ch.unit([4, 4, 6, 4], "mm")) cols_str = [str(c) for c in mat.columns] x_pos = (cols_str.index("1961") + 0.5) / len(cols_str) with ch.decorate_heatmap_body("cases"): ch.grid_lines([x_pos, x_pos], [0.0, 1.0], gp=ch.gpar(lwd=2, lty="dashed", col="#111111")) ch.grid_text( "Vaccine introduced (1961)", x=ch.unit(x_pos + 0.015, "npc"), y=ch.unit(1, "npc") + ch.unit(12, "mm"), just="left", gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=9.5, fontface="bold"), ) US measles incidence heatmap with marginal totals and 1961 vaccine marker

title:
14.3 Visualize cell heterogeneity from
single-cell RNA-seq
text: In this example, mouse T-cell single-cell RNA-seq data (data/mouse_scRNAseq_sample.csv) is filtered for genes expressed in over 50% of cells and correlated with at least 20 other signature genes (|Spearman rho| >= 0.5). Each gene is quantile-clamped (10%–90%) before z-scoring so outliers do not dominate the color scale. We align the scaled expression matrix (scaled_expr), mean expression (base_expr), ribonucleoprotein membership (data/mouse_ribonucleoprotein_genes.txt), cell-cycle membership (data/mouse_cell_cycle_genes.txt), anno_mark() gene labels, and the pairwise gene-gene correlation matrix (cor). Setting main_heatmap="cor" clusters all tracks according to the gene-gene correlation hierarchy, and decorate_column_dend() highlights the two primary cell subpopulations with translucent rectangles: from pathlib import Path import pandas as pd from scipy.stats import spearmanr expr = pd.read_csv("data/mouse_scRNAseq_sample.csv", index_col=0) expr = expr[(expr > 0).mean(axis=1) > 0.5] def get_correlated_variable_genes(df: pd.DataFrame, cor_cutoff: float = 0.5, n_cutoff: int = 20) -> pd.DataFrame: arr = df.to_numpy(dtype=float) scores = [] for i in range(arr.shape[0]): x = arr[i] q10, q90 = np.quantile(x, [0.1, 0.9]) sub = x[(x > q10) & (x < q90)] scores.append(float(np.var(sub, ddof=1) / np.mean(sub)) if len(sub) > 1 and np.mean(sub) > 0 else 0.0) mat_ord = df.iloc[np.argsort(scores)[::-1]] corr, _ = spearmanr(mat_ord.to_numpy(dtype=float), axis=1) np.fill_diagonal(corr, 0.0) return mat_ord.iloc[np.sum(np.abs(corr) >= cor_cutoff, axis=0) > n_cutoff] mat = get_correlated_variable_genes(expr, cor_cutoff=0.5, n_cutoff=20) mat_arr = mat.to_numpy(dtype=float) mat2 = np.empty_like(mat_arr) for i in range(mat_arr.shape[0]): x = np.clip(mat_arr[i], *np.quantile(mat_arr[i], [0.1, 0.9])) sd = np.std(x, ddof=1) mat2[i] = (x - np.mean(x)) / sd if sd > 0 else 0.0 mat2_df = pd.DataFrame(mat2, index=mat.index, columns=mat.columns) cc = set(Path("data/mouse_cell_cycle_genes.txt").read_text().splitlines()) rp = set(Path("data/mouse_ribonucleoprotein_genes.txt").read_text().splitlines()) ccl = np.array([g in cc for g in mat.index]) rpl = np.array([g in rp for g in mat.index]) base_mean = mat_arr.mean(axis=1) mark_idx = np.where(ccl & (base_mean > np.quantile(base_mean, 0.25)))[0].tolist() mark_labels = [str(mat.index[i]) for i in mark_idx] cor_mat = np.corrcoef(mat2) ht_list = ( ch.Heatmap( mat2_df, col=ch.colorRamp2([-1.5, 0, 1.5], ["blue", "white", "red"]), name="scaled_expr", column_title=f"relative expression for {mat.shape[0]} genes", show_column_names=False, show_row_names=False, width=ch.unit(8, "cm"), heatmap_legend_param={"title": "Scaled expr"}, ) + ch.Heatmap(base_mean, name="base_expr", width=ch.unit(5, "mm"), heatmap_legend_param={"title": "Base expr"}) + ch.Heatmap(rpl.astype(int), name="ribonucleoprotein", col={"0": "white", "1": "purple"}, show_heatmap_legend=False, width=ch.unit(5, "mm")) + ch.Heatmap(ccl.astype(int), name="cell_cycle", col={"0": "white", "1": "red"}, show_heatmap_legend=False, width=ch.unit(5, "mm")) + ch.rowAnnotation(link=ch.anno_mark(at=mark_idx, labels=mark_labels, labels_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=9.5), padding=ch.unit(1, "mm"))) + ch.Heatmap( cor_mat, name="cor", col=ch.colorRamp2([-1, 0, 1], ["green", "white", "red"]), show_row_names=False, show_column_names=False, row_dend_side="right", show_column_dend=False, column_title="pairwise correlation between genes", heatmap_legend_param={"title": "Correlation"}, ) ) ht_drawn = ch.draw(ht_list, width=12.5, height=8.0, main_heatmap="cor") tree = ch.column_dend(ht_drawn, name="scaled_expr") ind = ch.cutree(tree, k=2)[ch.order_dendrogram(tree)] n_cells = len(ind) with ch.decorate_column_dend("scaled_expr"): for grp, fill_col in zip((1, 2), ("#FF000040", "#00FF0040")): a = float(np.where(ind == grp)[0][0]) b = float(np.where(ind == grp)[0][-1] + 1) ch.grid_rect(x=ch.unit(a / n_cells, "npc"), width=ch.unit((b - a) / n_cells, "npc"), just="left", gp=ch.gpar(fill=fill_col, c

title:
14.4 Correlations between
methylation, expression and other genomic features
text: Using the bundled "meth" dataset (1,000 DMRs negatively correlated with nearest-gene expression across 10 tumor and 10 control samples), we synchronize column ordering across methylation and expression via column_order, split rows simultaneously by row_km=2 and row_split=direction, and merge all legends at the bottom: ds = ch.load_dataset("meth") mat_meth = ds["meth"].reset_index().to_numpy(dtype=float) mat_expr = ds["expr"].reset_index().to_numpy(dtype=float) anno_enhancer = ds["enhancer"].to_numpy(dtype=float) rm = ds["row_meta"].reset_index() direction = rm["direction"].tolist() cor_pvalue = rm["cor_pvalue"].to_numpy(dtype=float) gene_type = rm["gene_type"].tolist() anno_gene = rm["anno"].tolist() dist = rm["dist"].to_numpy(dtype=float) sample_type = ["Tumor"] * 10 + ["Control"] * 10 col_names = [f"sample{i}" for i in range(1, 21)] col_order = ch.hclust(ch.dist(mat_meth.T)).order gt_levels = list(dict.fromkeys(gene_type)) ag_levels = list(dict.fromkeys(anno_gene)) with ch.ht_opt.local( legend_title_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=8, fontface="bold"), legend_labels_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=8), heatmap_column_names_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=7.5), heatmap_column_title_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=10), heatmap_row_title_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=8), ): ha = ch.HeatmapAnnotation(type=sample_type, col={"type": {"Tumor": "pink", "Control": "royalblue"}}, annotation_name_side="left") ha2 = ch.HeatmapAnnotation(type=sample_type, col={"type": {"Tumor": "pink", "Control": "royalblue"}}, show_legend=False, show_annotation_name=False) ht_list = ( ch.Heatmap(pd.DataFrame(mat_meth, columns=col_names), name="methylation", col=ch.colorRamp2([0, 0.5, 1], ["blue", "white", "red"]), column_order=col_order, top_annotation=ha, column_title="Methylation", show_row_names=False, row_dend_width=ch.unit(8, "mm"), row_dend_gp=ch.gpar(lwd=0.4)) + ch.Heatmap(direction, name="direction", col={"hyper": "red", "hypo": "blue"}, title:
14.5 Visualize methylation profile
with complex annotations
text: This example reproduces the 12-track glioblastoma methylation overview from Sturm et al. (2012) by combining clinical/molecular metadata from data/450K_annotation.txt (136 DKFZ patients) with probe methylation, TSS distances, and chromatin-context CGI categories derived from ch.load_dataset("random_meth_expr_data"). Post-draw decorate_annotation() calls add custom right-aligned labels, frame borders, the age = 20 dashed threshold line, and section divider lines: ann_full = pd.read_csv("data/450K_annotation.txt", sep="\t", index_col=0, keep_default_na=False) pheno = ann_full.loc[[idx for idx in ann_full.index if str(idx).startswith("dkfz_")]].copy() ds = ch.load_dataset("random_meth_expr_data") base_meth = ds["mat_meth"].reset_index().to_numpy(dtype=float) row_meta = ds["row_meta"].reset_index() anno_states = ds["anno_states"] n_probes = 600 m2 = base_meth[:n_probes, 10:20] tss_dist = np.abs(row_meta["tss_dist"].to_numpy(dtype=float)[:n_probes]) st_arr = anno_states.iloc[:n_probes] cgi2 = np.where( st_arr["tss"].to_numpy() > 0.25, "Island", np.where(st_arr["enhancer"].to_numpy() > 0.15, "Shore", np.where(st_arr["repressive"].to_numpy() > 0.15, "Shelf", "OpenSea")), ) # Align probe profiles with the 6 DKFZ clinical subtypes in 450K_annotation.txt rng = title:
14.6 Add multiple boxplots for
single row
text: While anno_boxplot() draws one boxplot per row, wrapping grid_boxplot() inside an AnnotationFunction lets you draw paired or grouped boxplots inside each row viewport for direct visual comparison between two matrices: rng = np.random.default_rng(123) m1 = np.sort(rng.normal(size=(10, 10)), axis=1) m2 = np.sort(rng.normal(size=(10, 10)), axis=1)[:, ::-1] rg_lo = float(min(m1.min(), m2.min())) rg_hi = float(max(m1.max(), m2.max())) pad = (rg_hi - rg_lo) * 0.02 rg = (rg_lo - pad, rg_hi + pad) def anno_multiple_boxplot(index, k=1, n=1): nr = len(index) ch.pushViewport(ch.Viewport(xscale=rg, yscale=(0.5, nr + 0.5), clip=False)) try: for i, orig_i in enumerate(index): y_pos = nr - i ch.grid_rect(y=y_pos, height=1.0, default_units="native", gp=ch.gpar(fill="transparent", col="black")) ch.grid_boxplot(m1[orig_i], pos=y_pos + 0.2, box_width=0.3, gp=ch.gpar(fill="red"), direction="horizontal") ch.grid_boxplot(m2[orig_i], pos=y_pos - 0.2, box_width=0.3, gp=ch.gpar(fill="green"), direction="horizontal") ch.grid_xaxis() finally: ch.popViewport() anno_bp = ch.AnnotationFunction( fun=anno_multiple_boxplot, which="row", n=10, subsettable=True, width=ch.unit(4, "cm"), show_name=False ) ht_list = ch.Heatmap(m1, name="m1") + ch.Heatmap(m2, name="m2") + ch.rowAnnotation(boxplot=anno_bp, show_annotation_name=False) lgd = ch.Legend(labels=["m1", "m2"], title="boxplots", legend_gp=ch.gpar(fill=["red", "green"])) ch.draw(ht_list, padding=ch.unit([14, 2, 2, 2], "mm"), heatmap_legend_list=[lgd]) Paired horizontal boxplots per row via grid_boxplot and AnnotationFunction

title:
15.1 Set the same cell size for different heatmaps
with different dimensions
text: When exporting multiple heatmaps of different row or column counts to separate PNG or PDF files, you often want every cell to have the exact same physical dimensions (e.g., 5 mm × 5 mm). Because every non-body component in ComplexHeatmap-py (titles, dendrograms, annotations, axis labels, legends) has fixed physical size, the total figure height grows linearly with nr: height_in = a * nr + b. ht_size(ht, unit_name="inches", valueOnly=True) computes the exact total [width, height] of a Heatmap or HeatmapList layout without even needing to render pixels to disk. Testing two row counts (nr = 10 and nr = 20) recovers the exact slope (5 mm / 25.4 mm/in = 0.1969 in/row) and fixed overhead b: import numpy as np import pandas as pd import complexheatmap as ch def make_fixed_cell_heatmap(nr: int, title: str | None = None) -> ch.Heatmap: m = pd.DataFrame( np.random.default_rng(123 + nr).normal(size=(nr, 10)), index=[f"G{i + 1}" for i in range(nr)], columns=list("abcdefghij"), ) return ch.Heatmap( m, name="mat", height=ch.unit(5, "mm") * nr, width=ch.unit(5, "mm") * 10, column_title=title or f"{nr} rows, each row is 5 mm", top_annotation=ch.HeatmapAnnotation(bar=np.arange(1, 11)), ) xs = np.array([10.0, 20.0]) sizes = [ch.ht_size(make_fixed_cell_heatmap(int(nr), title="foo"), "inches", valueOnly=True) for nr in xs] heights_in = [s[1] for s in sizes] dev_w = max(s[0] for s in sizes) + 4.0 / 25.4 # add 4 mm horizontal page padding slope, intercept = np.polyfit(xs, heights_in, 1) print(f"height_in = {slope:.4f} * nr + {intercept:.4f}") # Output: height_in = 0.1969 * nr + 1.0770 Adding 4.0 / 25.4 inches (2 mm top + 2 mm bottom padding) to the figure height ensures both exported PNGs have identical 5 mm cell heights: pad_in = 4.0 / 25.4 for nr, out_name in ((10, "ch15_cell_size_10rows.png"), (20, "ch15_cell_size_20rows.png")): ht = make_fixed_cell_heatmap(nr, title=f"{nr} rows, each row is 5mm") ch.draw(ht, save=out_name, width=float(dev_w), height=float(slope * nr + intercept + pad_in), padding=ch.unit([2, 2, 2, 2], "mm")) 10-row heatmap exported at 5 mm per row 20-row heatmap exported with the exact same 5 mm per row cell height

title: 15.2 Global options with ht_opt
text: ht_opt stores package-wide styling defaults for borders, fonts, paddings, and clustering behavior. In Python, you can: Inspect all options with ht_opt(). Set global options persistently via ht_opt.heatmap_border = True or ht_opt(heatmap_border=True, ...). Scope temporary overrides safely using the with ht_opt.local(...): context manager (automatically restored on block exit). Reset all options back to defaults with ht_opt(RESET=True). rng = np.random.default_rng(42) m = pd.DataFrame(rng.normal(size=(10, 8)), index=[f"Gene{i + 1}" for i in range(10)], columns=[f"S{j + 1}" for j in range(8)]) ha = ch.HeatmapAnnotation( Group=["Ctrl"] * 4 + ["Treat"] * 4, Score=ch.anno_barplot(rng.uniform(0.2, 1.0, 8)), col={"Group": {"Ctrl": "#66C2A5", "Treat": "#FC8D62"}}, ) with ch.ht_opt.local( heatmap_border=True, annotation_border=True, heatmap_row_names_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=9, fontface="italic", col="#222222"), heatmap_column_names_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=9, fontface="bold"), heatmap_column_title_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=12, fontface="bold", col="#1B4F72"), legend_title_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=9, fontface="bold"), TITLE_PADDING=ch.unit([6, 2], "mm"), ): ht = ch.Heatmap( m, name="Z-score", top_annotation=ha, row_km=2, column_split=["Ctrl"] * 4 + ["Treat"] * 4, column_title="Styled with ht_opt.local(...)", ) ch.draw(ht, width=7.5, height=5.8) ch.ht_opt(RESET=True) Heatmap styled inside an ht_opt.local() context manager

title:
15.3 Capturing and composing heatmaps with
grid_grabExpr
text: When you need to arrange completely independent heatmaps (with unrelated rows and columns) into multi-panel figures—for instance, pairing a 2D expression heatmap in panel A with a 3D pathway activity heatmap in panel B—grid_grabExpr() records any draw(..., newpage=False) call into a replayable CapturedGrob that can be drawn inside arbitrary Viewport coordinates via grid_draw(): rng = np.random.default_rng(7) m1 = pd.DataFrame(rng.normal(size=(12, 8)), index=[f"R{i + 1}" for i in range(12)], columns=[f"A{j + 1}" for j in range(8)]) m2 = pd.DataFrame(rng.uniform(0, 10, size=(8, 6)), index=[f"P{i + 1}" for i in range(8)], columns=[f"B{j + 1}" for j in range(6)]) ht_a = ch.Heatmap( m1, name="Expr", col=ch.colorRamp2([-2, 0, 2], ["#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"]), column_title="Panel A: Z-score Expression", row_km=2, row_names_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=8), column_names_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=8), ) ht_b = ch.Heatmap3D( m2, name="Score", col=ch.colorRamp2([0, 5, 10], ["#FFFFCC", "#FD8D3C", "#BD0026"]), column_title="Panel B: 3D Pathway Activity", top_annotation=ch.HeatmapAnnotation(_spacer=ch.anno_empty(border=False, height=ch.unit(6, "mm")), show_annotation_name=False), bar_max_length=ch.unit(7, "mm"), row_names_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=8), column_names_gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=8), ) grob_a = ch.grid_grabExpr(lambda: ch.draw(ht_a, padding=ch.unit([3, 3, 3, 3], "mm"), newpage=False), width_in=5.5, height_in=5.0) grob_b = ch.grid_grabExpr(lambda: ch.draw(ht_b, padding=ch.unit([3, 3, 5, 5], "mm"), newpage=False), width_in=5.5, height_in=5.0) dev = ch.grid_newpage(width_in=11.0, height_in=5.0, dpi=140) ch.grid_rect(gp=ch.gpar(fill="white", col=None)) ch.pushViewport(ch.Viewport(x=ch.unit(0.0, "npc"), y=ch.unit(0.0, "npc"), width=ch.unit(0.5, "npc"), height=ch.unit(1.0, "npc"), just=("left", "bottom"))) ch.grid_draw(grob_a) ch.grid_text("A", x=ch.unit(4, "mm"), y=ch.unit(1, "npc") - ch.unit(4, "mm"), just=("left", "top"), gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=14, fontface="bold")) ch.popViewport() ch.pushViewport(ch.Viewport(x=ch.unit(0.5, "npc"), y=ch.unit(0.0, "npc"), width=ch.unit(0.5, "npc"), height=ch.unit(1.0, "npc"), just=("left", "bottom"))) ch.grid_draw(grob_b) ch.grid_text("B", x=ch.unit(4, "mm"), y=ch.unit(1, "npc") - ch.unit(4, "mm"), just=("left", "top"), gp=ch.gpar(fontsize=14, fontface="bold")) ch.popViewport() dev.fig.savefig("ch15_grid_grab_compose.png", dpi=140, facecolor="white") Multi-panel figure combining a 2D heatmap and a 3D heatmap via grid_grabExpr

Splitting genes at an amplification rate threshold of 10% highlights that highly amplified genes enrich in cellular response processes whereas predominantly mutated genes cluster into developmental and metabolic pathways. import re import numpy as np import pandas as pd import complexheatmap as ch from complexheatmap import ( Heatmap, HeatmapAnnotation, anno_barplot, anno_points, anno_text, title:
16.2.2 Figure 1B: Mouse T-Cell Single-Cell
RNA-seq Heterogeneity Across 721 Signature Genes
text: Figure 1B reproduces the full 721-gene x 81-cell mouse T-cell single-cell RNA-seq analysis from Buettner et al. (2015). Because main_heatmap="cor" is specified in draw(), hierarchical clustering of the 721 x 721 pairwise gene-correlation matrix controls the row ordering of every parallel heatmap and annotation (scaled_expr, base_expr, ribonucleoprotein, cell_cycle, and anno_mark). Post-draw decorate_column_dend() highlights the two cellular subpopulations (G2/M cell-cycle-active cells on the left vs ribonucleoprotein-enriched cells on the right). import numpy as np import pandas as pd import complexheatmap as ch from complexheatmap import ( Heatmap, anno_mark, colorRamp2, decorate_column_dend, gpar, grid_rect, rowAnnotation, unit, ) mat_df = pd.read_csv("data/pub2016_fig1b_scrna721.csv", index_col=0) mat_arr = mat_df.to_numpy(dtype=float) # Winsorize per gene to [10th, 90th] percentiles before z-scaling mat2 = np.empty_like(mat_arr) for i in range(mat_arr.shape[0]): x = np.clip(mat_arr[i], *np.quantile(mat_arr[i], [0.1, 0.9])) sd = np.std(x, ddof=1) mat2[i] = (x - np.mean(x)) / sd if sd > 0 else 0.0 mat2_df = pd.DataFrame(mat2, index=mat_df.index, columns=mat_df.columns) cc_set = set(open("data/mouse_cell_cycle_genes.txt").read().splitlines()) rp_set = set(open("data/mouse_ribonucleoprotein_genes.txt").read().splitlines()) ccl = np.array([g in cc_set for g in mat_df.index]) rpl = np.array([g in rp_set for g in mat_df.index]) base_mean = mat_arr.mean(axis=1) mark_idx = np.where(ccl & (base_mean > np.quantile(base_mean, 0.25)))[0].tolist() mark_labels = [str(mat_df.index[i]) for i in mark_idx] cor_mat = np.corrcoef(mat2) ht_list = ( Heatmap( mat2_df, col=colorRamp2([-1.5, 0, 1.5], ["blue", "white", "red"]), name="scaled_expr", column_title=f"relative expression for {mat_df.shape[0]} genes", show_column_names=False, show_row_names=False, width=unit(7.6, "cm"), heatmap_legend_param={"title": "Scaled expr"}, use_raster=True, ) + Heatmap(base_mean, name="base_expr", width=unit(4.5, "mm"), heatmap_legend_param={"title": "Base expr"}) + Heatmap(rpl.astype(int), name="ribonucleoprotein", col={"0": "white", "1": "purple"}, show_heatmap_legend=False, width=unit(4.5, "mm")) + Heatmap(ccl.astype(int), name="cell_cycle", col={"0": "white", "1": "red"}, show_heatmap_legend=False, width=unit(4.5, "mm")) + rowAnnotation(link=anno_mark(at=mark_idx, labels=mark_labels, labels_gp=gpar(fontsize=7.5), link_width=unit(6, "mm"))) + Heatmap( cor_mat, name="cor", col=colorRamp2([-1, 0, 1], ["green", "white", "red"]), show_row_names=False, show_column_names=False, row_dend_side="right", show_column_dend=False, column_title="pairwise correlation between genes", heatmap_legend_param={"title": "Correlation"}, use_raster=True, ) ) ht_drawn = ch.draw(ht_list, main_heatmap="cor") tree = ch.column_dend(ht_drawn, name="scaled_expr") ind = ch.cutree(tree, k=2)[ch.order_dendrogram(tree)] with decorate_column_dend("scaled_expr"): for grp_id, fill_col in zip((1, 2), ("#FF000040", "#00FF0040")): pos = np.where(ind == grp_id)[0] grid_rect(x=unit(pos[0] / len(ind), "npc"), width=unit((pos[-1] - pos[0] + 1) / len(ind), "npc"), just="left", gp=gpar(fill=fill_col, col=None)) Bioinformatics 2016 Figure 1B reproduction: 721-gene mouse T-cell scRNA-seq + correlation

title:
16.3 iMeta (2022): Complex Heatmap
Visualization
text: Gu, Z. (2022). Complex heatmap visualization. iMeta, 1(3), e43. DOI: 10.1002/imt2.43.

title: 16.3.1 Figure 1: Modular Object-Oriented Design
text: Figure 1 illustrates the three core classes shared by ComplexHeatmap and ComplexHeatmap-py: (A) Heatmap: Central sliced matrix body surrounded on all four sides by titles, dendrograms, dimension labels, and heatmap annotations. (B) HeatmapAnnotation: A stack of SingleAnnotation tracks. (C) HeatmapList: A horizontal (+) or vertical (%v%) container aligning multiple heatmaps and annotations inside shared global titles and legends. from complexheatmap import Viewport, grid_rect, grid_text, popViewport, pushViewport, gpar, unit # Uses Viewport + grid_rect + grid_text inside grid_newpage() # Full helper implementation in scripts/ch16_publication_examples.py::render_2022_fig1_design() iMeta 2022 Figure 1 reproduction: Modular design of ComplexHeatmap-py

title:
16.3.2 Figure 2: Single Heatmap Annotations, Body
Customization, and Subgroup Splitting
text: Panel A: Combines color_branches(dend, k=3) and custom node_par glyphs on column dendrograms, combined categorical + k-means row splitting (row_split=["A", "B"] * 9, row_km=2), anno_points (decorate_annotation baseline at 0.5), and stacked anno_barplot with a custom Legend. Panel B: Uses layer_fun with restore_matrix(j, i, x, y) to connect adjacent same-sign cells via grid_segments() + grid_points() and highlight off-diagonal slice blocks (if kr != kc). import numpy as np import pandas as pd import complexheatmap as ch from complexheatmap import ( Heatmap, HeatmapAnnotation, Legend, anno_barplot, anno_points, colorRamp2, color_branches, decorate_annotation, gpar, grid_lines, grid_points, grid_rect, grid_segments, restore_matrix, rowAnnotation, unit, ) rng = np.random.default_rng(123) mat = np.hstack([ np.vstack([rng.normal(1, 0.5, (4, 6)), rng.normal(0, 0.5, (8, 6)), rng.normal(0, 0.5, (6, 6))]), np.vstack([rng.normal(0, 0.5, (4, 8)), rng.normal(1, 0.5, (8, 8)), rng.normal(0, 0.5, (6, 8))]), np.vstack([rng.normal(0.5, 0.5, (4, 10)), rng.normal(0.5, 0.5, (8, 10)), rng.normal(1, 0.5, (6, 10))]), ])[rng.permutation(18), :][:, rng.permutation(24)] col_dend = color_branches(ch.as_dendrogram(ch.hclust(ch.dist(mat.T))), k=3) ht_a = Heatmap( mat, name="mat", row_dend_width=unit(1.8, "cm"), cluster_columns=col_dend, show_column_names=False, row_split=["A", "B"] * 9, row_km=2, column_split=3, top_annotation=HeatmapAnnotation(foo1=np.arange(1, 25), bar1=anno_points(rng.uniform(size=24))), right_annotation=rowAnnotation(foo2=np.arange(18, 0, -1), bar2=anno_barplot(rng.uniform(size=(18, 2)), gp=gpar(fill=["#DF536B", "#61D04F"]), width=unit(2, "cm"))), ) small_mat = mat[:9, :9] def layer_b(j, i, x, y, w, h, fill, kr, kc): ind_mat = restore_matrix(j, i, x, y) for ir in range(ind_mat.shape[0]): for ic in range(1, ind_mat.shape[1]): p1, p2 = int(ind_mat[ir, ic - 1]), int(ind_mat[ir, ic]) v1, v2 = small_mat[int(i[p1]), int(j[p1])], small_mat[int(i[p2]), int(j[p2])] if v1 * v2 > 0: c_line = "violet" if v1 > 0 else "blue" grid_segments(x[p1], y[p1], x[p2], y[p2], gp=gpar(col=c_line, lwd=1.8)) grid_points(x[[p1, p2]], y[[p1, p2]], pch=16, size=unit(2.6, "mm"), gp=gpar(col=c_line)) if kr != kc: grid_rect(gp=gpar(lwd=2.2, fill="transparent", col="black")) ht_b = Heatmap(small_mat, name="mat_b", col=colorRamp2([-2, 0, 2], ["green", "white", "red"]), row_km=2, column_km=2, layer_fun=layer_b) iMeta 2022 Figure 2A-B reproduction: Dendrogram styling, splitting, and layer_fun Panels C & D contrast global column clustering vs pre-splitting columns by TCGA Glioblastoma consensus subgroup (class 1..4, with TCGA subtype tracks along the bottom): pre-splitting prevents subgroups with moderate differences (class 3 vs 4) from mixing in a single global dendrogram. expr_df = pd.read_csv("data/pub2022_fig2cd_expr.csv", index_col=0) meta_df = pd.read_csv("data/pub2022_fig2cd_meta.csv") cls_vec = [str(c) for c in meta_df["class"]] sub_vec = [str(s) for s in meta_df["subtype"]] # Panel D: pre-split columns by consensus class and cluster genes into 4 blocks ht_d = Heatmap( expr_df, name="mat", col=colorRamp2([-2, 0, 2], ["green", "white", "red"]), row_km=4, column_split=pd.Categorical(cls_vec, categories=["1", "2", "3", "4"], ordered=True), show_row_names=False, show_row_dend=False, show_column_names=False, top_annotation=HeatmapAnnotation(**{"class": cls_vec}), bottom_annotation=HeatmapAnnotation(subtype=sub_vec), use_raster=True, ) iMeta 2022 Figure 2C-D reproduction: TCGA GBM global clustering vs pre-split by class

title:
16.3.3 Figure 3: Built-in and Complex Heatmap Annotation
Gallery
text: Figure 3A renders 13 distinct annotation types side by side in ComplexHeatmap-py: anno_simple, anno_image, anno_points, anno_lines, anno_lines(..., smooth=True), anno_barplot, anno_numeric (percent bars), anno_boxplot, anno_text(gt_render(...)), anno_histogram, anno_density(..., type="violin"), anno_joyplot, and anno_horizon. iMeta 2022 Figure 3A reproduction: 13-track annotation graphics gallery Figures 3B–D showcase complex structural annotations linked to heatmap slices: anno_mark callout labels for sparse gene subsets (B), anno_link attaching custom vertical grouped-boxplot panels to k-means row slices (C), and anno_textbox drawing importance-sized word clouds alongside slice blocks (D). # Pattern for Panel C (anno_link on split heatmap) and Panel D (anno_textbox): ht_c = ( Heatmap(mat, name="mat_c", row_split=km_cat, column_split=group_cat, cluster_column_slices=False) + rowAnnotation(link=anno_link(align_to=ind_list, which="row", panel_fun=panel_boxplot, size=unit(2.1, "cm"), width=unit(4.6, "cm"))) ) ht_d = ( Heatmap(mat_d, name="mat_d", cluster_rows=False, row_split=split_cat) + rowAnnotation(wc=anno_textbox(split_d, text_d, max_width=unit(6.6, "cm"))) ) iMeta 2022 Figure 3B-D reproduction: anno_mark, anno_link boxplots, and anno_textbox word clouds

title:
16.3.4 Figure 4: Multi-Omics Heatmap Lists and Global
Epigenomic Summary
text: Figure 4A integrates DNA methylation (Methylation), DMR direction (hyper/hypo), paired gene expression (Expression), -log10 Pearson correlation p-value, gene biotype, genomic context, genomic distance to TSS (anno_points), and enhancer overlap across 1,000 DMRs using ch.load_dataset("meth"). Notice that hypomethylated promoter clusters (2,hypo, bottom-left) concentrate at low TSS distance (0–5 kb) and overlap enhancers strongly. ds = ch.load_dataset("meth") mat_meth = ds["meth"].to_numpy(dtype=float) mat_expr = ds["expr"].to_numpy(dtype=float) anno_enhancer = ds["enhancer"].to_numpy(dtype=float) rm = ds["row_meta"] direction = rm["direction"].tolist() # See scripts/ch16_publication_examples.py::render_2022_fig4a_meth_list() for full setup iMeta 2022 Figure 4A reproduction: Multi-omics methylation, expression, TSS distance, and enhancer list Figure 4B aggregates global summary statistics across four glioblastoma subgroup DMR sets (hyper1..4 and hypo1..4) from ch.load_dataset("dmr_summary"), combining mean methylation heatmaps, DMR count barplots, stacked compositional tracks (correlation direction, TSS distance bins, gene/CGI overlap, ChromHMM chromatin state fractions), and enrichment Z-score heatmaps. iMeta 2022 Figure 4B reproduction: Global epigenomic summary statistics across 9 tracks

title:
16.3.5 Figure 5: High-Level Genomic and Statistical
Plots
text: Figure 5 demonstrates the five built-in high-level Heatmap specializations in ComplexHeatmap-py: Panels A & B: densityHeatmap() and 3D frequencyHeatmap(..., use_3d=True) comparing 10 normal (rnorm) and 10 uniform (runif) columns annotated by Distribution. dh = densityHeatmap(df, ylab="Value", top_annotation=ha, title="A) Density heatmap") fh3d = frequencyHeatmap(df, ylab="Value", top_annotation=ha, use_3d=True, title="B) 3D frequency heatmap", bar_max_length=unit(7, "mm")) iMeta 2022 Figure 5A-B reproduction: densityHeatmap and 3D frequencyHeatmap Panel C: oncoPrint() for 22 RAS–RAF–MEK–JNK signaling genes across 80 TCGA Lung Adenocarcinoma samples (ch.load_dataset("tcga_lung_adenocarcinoma")). iMeta 2022 Figure 5C reproduction: TCGA Lung Adenocarcinoma RAS-RAF-MEK-JNK OncoPrint Panel D: Genomic UpSet() plot quantifying base-pair overlaps (CombMat built from Roadmap Epigenomics H3K4me3 ChIP-seq peaks across 6 tissues: Brain, ESC, Heart, Muscle, ES-deriv2, ES-deriv1), formatted directly in megabases (MB). sets_df = pd.read_csv("data/pub2022_fig5d_h3k4me3_sets.csv") combs_df = pd.read_csv("data/pub2022_fig5d_h3k4me3_combs.csv", dtype={"comb_code": str}) cm = CombMat( mat=combs_df[sets_df["set_name"].tolist()].to_numpy(dtype=int).T, set_names=sets_df["set_name"].tolist(), comb_codes=combs_df["comb_code"].tolist(), set_sizes=sets_df["set_size"].to_numpy(dtype=float), comb_sizes=combs_df["comb_size"].to_numpy(dtype=float), mode="distinct", ) up = UpSet( cm, set_order=np.argsort(-cm.set_size()).tolist(), comb_order=np.argsort(-cm.comb_size()).tolist(), top_annotation=upset_top_annotation(cm, height=unit(3.6, "cm"), axis_param={"at": [0, 1e7, 2e7], "labels": ["0 MB", "10 MB", "20 MB"]}), right_annotation=upset_right_annotation(cm, width=unit(2.8, "cm"), annotation_name_offset=unit(8, "mm"), axis_param={"at": [0, 2e7, 4e7, 6e7], "labels": ["0", "20", "40", "60 MB"], "side": "bottom", "labels_rot": 0}), ) iMeta 2022 Figure 5D reproduction: Genomic UpSet plot of Roadmap H3K4me3 peaks Panel E: Genome-scale vertical (% v %) multi-track heatmap across chr1..chr22 (bin_genome("hg19", bin_size=1_000_000) + normalize_genomic_signals_to_bins()) stacking subgroup (A/B) signals, categorical CNV calls (gain/loss), anno_mark gene loci, anno_points, and anno_barplot in one aligned coordinate system. iMeta 2022 Figure 5E reproduction: Genome-level multi-track vertical heatmap across chr1..chr22

title:
16.3.6 Figure 6: TSS Spatial Enrichment Profiles
(EnrichedHeatmap Equivalent in ComplexHeatmap-py)
text: In the iMeta (2022) paper, Figure 6 demonstrates how ComplexHeatmap serves as an extensible foundation for companion packages — specifically R’s EnrichedHeatmap (anno_enriched() + EnrichedHeatmap()). While EnrichedHeatmap itself is a separate R/Bioconductor package, its spatial TSS visualization maps naturally onto native ComplexHeatmap-py primitives: aligned -5000..+5000 bp matrix heatmaps (States, Methylation), a 1-column Expression heatmap with anno_summary(), and custom top metaplot profile annotations (AnnotationFunction) comparing active, bivalent, and inactive promoters across 600 Roadmap E003 TSSs (data/pub2022_fig6_tss_roadmap.npz). npz = np.load("data/pub2022_fig6_tss_roadmap.npz") states_str = np.asarray([str(s) for s in npz["state_names"]], dtype=object)[npz["states_idx"]] meth, expr = npz["meth"], npz["expr"] split_ord = pd.Categorical([str(g) for g in npz["group"]], categories=["active", "bivalent", "inactive"], ordered=True) # Top summary metaplot lines (solid=active, dashed=bivalent, dotted=inactive) + aligned heatmaps ht_list = ht_states + ht_meth + ht_expr ch.draw(ht_list, ht_gap=unit(10, "mm"), column_title="Visualize chromatin states, methylation and expression", heatmap_legend_list=[lgd_cat]) iMeta 2022 Figure 6 reproduction: Chromatin states, DNA methylation (-5kb..+5kb TSS), and expression
